question: The Fragas do Eume nature reserve (Galicia) is a Special Area of Conservation (SAC) in the Natura 2000 network. The Usage and Management Plans (PRUX) of the seven nature reserves in Galicia’s Natura Network were completed in 2023 (amending the 1996 plan). The plans mobilise EUR 70 million of European funding, with the regional government providing EUR 3 million.

Together with staff costs, this reaches a total of EUR 8.5 million over ten years1. In 2023, the regional government declared the Fragas do Eume Foundation – established by Ecoener – to be in the regional interest. Ecoener is a multinational corporation offering environmental engineering solutions. It is listed on the stock exchange.
According to the information available, at least part of the management of the funds for the reserve has been awarded to this multinational2. In view of this: 1.
To which entity are the European funds ultimately being allocated?
What information does the Commission have on the plans and their implementation and who is responsible for implementing and ensuring the proper use of these funds since the SAC’s creation?
Are there any cases where SACs belong to several neighbours or owners and where these receive compensation on account of new usage limitations and who should provide such compensation?

Regional Government of Galicia, Galician Government approves the 10-year Usage and Management Plan for the Fragas do Eume Nature Reserve entailing an estimated investment of EUR 8.5 million: https://www.xunta.gal/notas-de-prensa/-/nova/77757/rueda-anuncia-que-xunta-aprueba-plan-uso-gestion-delparque-natural-fragas-eume?

answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.4.2024) 1&2. Various EU funds can support the Natura 2000 network. The Spanish Common Agriculture Policy (CAP) Strategic Plan 2023-20271 and also the interventions financed by the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development2 under the Rural Development Plan of Galicia 2014-2022 are administered under the shared management principle.

The management and implementation lie with the Members States, in compliance with EU legislation. This principle also applies to the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF)3, where Member States are responsible for project selection, within the objectives of the programmes (OP). ‘Fragas do Eume’ has benefited from EUR 850,126.

82 co-financed by the 2014-2020 ERDF OP of Galicia through operations to promote the natural heritage. The funds were allocated to the Directorate-General for Natural Heritage of Galicia. According to the managing authority of the 2014-2020 ERDF programme of Galicia, Ecoener and Fragas de Eume Foundation have not been beneficiaries of any operation financed by the ERDF on this site.

Spain publishes the management plans of Special Areas of Conservation (SAC) and other protected areas in their official journals. The adoption and implementation of the ‘Fragas do Eume’ plan4 is under the responsibility of the authorities of Galicia.

The Commission is following up an infringement procedure5 against Spain concerning the designation of SACs and the set-up of conservation objectives and measures in its SACs, including in Galicia. 3. SACs may be designated on private lands and involve several landowners.
It is up to the competent authorities to take decisions as regards a possible compensation of owners for uselimitations and the financial source for such compensation.
